name: Shillong
description: Capital city of Meghalaya and headquarters of East Khasi Hills, known as the Scotland of the East for its pine-covered hills, pleasant climate, and colonial charm.
facts: Named after U Lei Shillong deity

name: Krang Suri Falls
description: Stunning turquoise waterfall in Amlarem sub-division of West Jaintia Hills, cascading into a clear natural pool amid limestone cliffs and dense forest.

name: Moopun Waterfalls
description: 110-foot high and 50-foot wide waterfall on the Umjhai River at Mutong village in East Jaintia Hills, featuring a unique stone bridge above the falls and rare pitcher plants growing on the rock face. Cascades into a crystal-clear natural pool.
facts: About 25 km from both Jowai and Khliehriat
Short 5-minute walk from parking to base
Connected by legend to Umhang Lake

name: Krem Liat Prah
description: Longest natural cave in India and South Asia, located on the Shnongrim Ridge in East Jaintia Hills. Explored length about 34 km with massive trunk passages like the Aircraft Hangar; part of a larger limestone cave system.

name: Umhang Lake
description: Largest and most revered lake in the Jaintia Hills, located near Bataw village. Formed by Chieftain U Sajar Nangli; sacred to locals who offer annual sacrifices. Surrounded by dense forest.
facts: Near Bataw village, about 30 km from Khliehriat
Created by Chieftain U Sajar Nangli
Connected by legend to Moopun Falls

name: Rynji Falls
description: Roaring waterfall in Cham Cham village, East Jaintia Hills, featuring stepping natural ponds above the cascade. Ideal for eco-trekking and angling; well-connected with footpaths through the forest.
facts: About 3 km south of Mutong/Moopun Falls

name: Umbyrlein Falls
description: Majestic offbeat waterfall in Rangad Village, cascading into a large natural pool. Accessible via short trek through meadows with menhirs, swings, and gazebos offering panoramic views.
facts: 36 km from Jowai, 7 km from Kongong junction on NH6

name: Sahksaw Fish Sanctuary
description: Tranquil community fish sanctuary at Cham Cham village on a meandering stretch of the river, ideal for boating. Surrounded by lofty hills; abundant fish and fresh water from catchment areas.
facts: 700 metres from PWD road in Cham Cham
Best for boating in East Jaintia Hills

name: Borghat Temple
description: Historic Shiva temple in Borghat village near the Bangladesh border, built by Jaintia kings. Damaged by the 1897 earthquake; features brick architecture and remains a site of quiet pilgrimage.
facts: Built by Jaintia kings who embraced Hinduism

name: Moolamylliang Village
description: Village in Saipung Block of East Jaintia Hills promoted for adventure, natural beauty, and recreational tourism. Offers authentic rural experiences amid the hills.

name: Lumchyrmit Village
description: Relatively new and unexplored tourist spot located 10 km from Cham Cham Village in East Jaintia Hills, suited for adventure and nature enthusiasts seeking quiet trails.
facts: New tourist spot per official listing

name: Khliehriat
description: Headquarters and main town of East Jaintia Hills district, serving as the administrative and transport hub for exploring the region's caves, waterfalls, and villages. Base for taxis to remote sites.
facts: District HQ of East Jaintia Hills since 2012

name: Nartiang Monoliths
description: Largest collection of megalithic stones in one area in Meghalaya, north of Nartiang market in West Jaintia Hills. Erected between 1500-1835 AD by Jaintia clans and kings as memorials.
facts: Biggest collection of monoliths in one area
Near summer palace ruins of Jaintia kings

name: Nartiang Durga Temple
description: 600-year-old Shakti Peeth temple dedicated to Durga in Nartiang village, West Jaintia Hills. Built by Jaintia kings adjacent to summer palace ruins; one of the 51 Shakti Peethas.
facts: Adjacent to Jaintia summer palace ruins

name: Thadlaskein Lake
description: Man-made historical lake near Mukhla village in West Jaintia Hills, also called Pung Sajar Nangli. Dug by followers of rebel general Sajar Nangli; ideal for boating and picnics.

name: Dawki / Umngot River
description: Border town and crystal-clear Umngot River in West Jaintia Hills near India-Bangladesh border. Famous for glass-like water where boats appear to float, and 1932 suspension bridge.

name: Shnongpdeng
description: Riverside village upstream from Dawki on the Umngot River in West Jaintia Hills. Popular for camping, kayaking, cliff jumping, and quieter crystal-clear water experiences.

name: Tyrshi Falls
description: Scenic multi-tiered waterfall about 5-8 km from Jowai in West Jaintia Hills, accessible via arch bridge over paddy fields with panoramic valley views.
facts: Three times taller than Elephant Falls

name: Syntu Ksiar
description: Riverside meadow and historical site on Myntdu River near Jowai, meaning 'Golden Flower'. Site of U Kiang Nangbah freedom struggle monument and calm waters.

name: Ialong Park
description: Ecological park about 8 km from Jowai offering views of Pynthor Wah valley and Myntdu River, with sacred grove elements.

name: Phe Phe Falls
description: Two-tiered offbeat waterfall near Shkentalang/Jarain in West Jaintia Hills with turquoise plunge pool, reached by short trek through forest.

name: Jowai
description: Headquarters of West Jaintia Hills district, cultural and commercial hub of the Pnar people on a plateau surrounded by Myntdu River.
facts: District HQ of West Jaintia Hills
